verdict.rationale: HelixDB documents a public HTTP API that accepts operation-tree queries at POST /v2/query, available on both local servers and the Helix Cloud gateway. It uses Bearer-token auth with scoped API keys, ships official typed SDKs in Rust, TypeScript, Go and Python, and a probe confirmed a published openapi.json spec. Community complaints about the query language concern ergonomics rather than whether the API exists, so they do not create a dispute. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of driving the API end-to-end, and documented HTTP-API coverage of administrative (non-query) operations beyond the CLI/MCP.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The HelixDB HTTP API accepts operation-tree queries at `POST /v2/query`. The same contract is available from a local server and a Helix Cloud gateway.
All API requests to Helix Cloud are authenticated with a Bearer token.
HelixDB v3 uses one operation-tree request model across the Rust, TypeScript, Go, and Python SDKs.
Scoped API keys with read-only, read-write, or operation-restricted permissions for least-privilege credentials per service or environment.
